rows.note: This is the all-purpose possessive form, used predicatively or with the possessed noun omitted.

example.jyutping: ni1 baa2 ze1 hai6 ngo5 ge3

rows.note: Use this for the all-purpose land-based explosive mine.

example.english: There is a mine on this road, so don't walk over there.
example.traditional: 呢條路有地雷，唔好行過去。
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 lou6 jau5 dei6 leoi4 m4 hou2 haang4 gwo3 heoi3

rows.note: Use this specifically for a naval or underwater explosive mine.

example.english: The warship has to watch out for a mine.
example.jyutping: gwan1 laam6 jiu3 siu2 sam1 seoi2 leoi4

rows.note: Use this colloquial form specifically for “my place” or “my home,” especially in location expressions such as 喺我度.

example.english: Come to mine for dinner tonight.
example.jyutping: nei5 gam1 maan5 lai4 ngo5 dou6 sik6 faan6 laa1

rows.note: Use this for a physical site where ore or minerals are extracted.

example.english: I visited a mine when I was little.
example.jyutping: ngo5 sai3 go3 go2 zan6 heoi3 gwo3 kwong3 coeng4

rows.note: Use this figuratively for a person or source rich in information or other valuable resources.

example.english: This book is a mine of knowledge.
example.jyutping: ni1 bun2 syu1 zan1 hai6 zi1 sik1 bou2 fu3
